ai.description: This 30–40 mm frog is brownish-grey with distinct skin folds. It features a pointed snout, prominent toe discs, and a characteristic white patch on the throat. It inhabits fast-flowing forest streams.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus vasanthi* is distinguished by its unique, extremely elongated third finger, which is significantly longer than the others, unlike any other Indian wrinkled frog.
ai.habitat: The Kalakad wrinkled frog inhabits high-altitude evergreen rainforests in the Southern Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at elevations above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kalakad wrinkled frog is primarily nocturnal and exhibits unique parental care, with males guarding egg clutches laid on moss-covered rocks near streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus vasanthi* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs in rock crevices or stream-side vegetation for direct development.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Kalakad wrinkled frog is endemic to the southern Western Ghats, specifically occurring in the Kalakad-Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve of Tamil Nadu at high elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Kalakad Wrinkled Frog produces a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "chirp-like" notes, typically heard emanating from rocky, fast-flowing streams in its forest habitat.
